correctness.rationale: Each circular factor of length≤n occurs in a rotation of the length-n word. Published linear run lemmas for 3, 4 and 5 runs force cyclic two-run parity, four-run singleton alternation, and ≥6-run alternation via sliding five-run windows. Alternating factors cannot be nontrivial half conjugates. Necklace counts use distinct ordered zero/one run lengths, full period n for two-run circles and period two for alternating words; n=1,2 overlap is handled. Independent direct factor and conjugate check matches 32,766 binary words at lengths 1..14, without treating finite enumeration as infinite proof.

evidence: Published theorems cover arbitrary linear words and infinite one-sided avoiding sequences, both different quantifier domains.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Linear inclusion cannot directly imply exact number of rotations simultaneously satisfying the condition; infinite periodic avoidance is strictly stronger than bounded one turn.

evidence: The all-length linear classification is in the 2021 preprint; cyclic compatibility across every rotation is an intersection problem.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The claim is equivalent to characterizing linear avoiders stable under all rotations, but prior text does not supply the cyclic compatibility solution.

exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No exact cyclic N_n=4/n/2+3 table among the inspected sources; the OEIS table does not dominate the result.

originality.rationale: Cummings–Shallit–Staadecker 2021 gives full linear binary mesosome avoidance and run lemmas, which are explicitly imported. It does not state the all-rotations one-turn cyclic parity classification or exact necklace counts. OEIS A341277 counts linear mesosome-free strings, not cyclic equivalence classes. An existing cyclic corollary of that linear theorem remains possible.
residual_risks: A pre-existing cyclic version or simple corollary of the full linear theorem could cover the result in other work.
Finite independent check stops at n=14; all-length result depends on the cited run lemmas and proof.

value.rationale: Passing from linear to bounded one-turn circular factors creates a sharp parity collapse: exactly four necklaces at all odd lengths and linear growth at even lengths. This is a natural complete all-length cyclic classification rather than arbitrary finite census; the one-turn qualification distinguishes it from infinite periodic avoidance.

checked_sources: Resultary semantic search on full claim (current run)
final_claim: For binary one-turn mesosome-free circular words, necklaces are exactly constants, two-run circles with a singleton run or both odd run lengths, and even alternating circles; N_n=4 (odd n≥3), N_n=n/2+3 (even n≥4), with L_n=2+2n and n²/2+4 respectively and n=1,2 exceptions.
limitations: Binary alphabet and circular factors of length at most one circumference, not all factors in infinite periodic repetition.
residual_risks: A pre-existing cyclic version or simple corollary of the full linear theorem could cover the result in other work.
Finite independent check stops at n=14; all-length result depends on the cited run lemmas and proof.
